newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli shares rise on shekel's decline.
newsitem.headline: Israeli shares rise on shekel's decline.

text.p: Israeli shares closed broadly higher on Sunday for the fourth consecutive session following the shekel's decline against the dollar and hopes for an interest rate cut, traders said.

The benchmark Mishtanim index of the top 100 shares gained 1.26 percent, or 2.38 points, to 191.58 on low turnover of 60 million shekels against 62 million on Thursday, the last day of trading before the Israeli weekend.
The Maof 25 blue chip index rose 1.22 percent to 201.99.
"The market is rising because of the shekel's decline and hopes for an interest rate cut. But, activity is still very low," said Amir Eyal at Epsilon Securities.

The Israeli shekel lost more than two percent against the dollar on Thursday and Friday on hopes that the Bank of Israel would make a significant reduction in short-term rates. The central bank will announce interest rates for November on October 28. The key short-term rate is now 15.5 percent.

"Many companies are repaying their dollar-linked loans, and I believe the shekel will continue to decline in the coming days. A combination of a shekel depreciation and an interest rate cut is good for the market," Eyal said.
The main gainer on the Maof was Elco Industries, which surged 5.5 percent to 9,259. Traders said the share rose on very low volume of less than 50,000 shekels.
"The dollar's rise and the expectations for a rate cut are pushing the market. But its difficult to predict by how much will the central bank cut the rate," said a trader at Bank Leumi.
"After the rise in the money supply it's hard to belive that the central bank will lower the rate by more than 0.3-0.5 percentage points," she said.

The Bank of Israel said on Sunday that M1 money supply expanded 1.7 percent to a prelminary 16.86 billion shekels in September following a drop of 0.3 percent in August. In the first nine months of the year, the money supply grew 11.1 percent.

The most active shares were Koor Industries, which gained 2.75 percent to 29,940 on volume of 3.2 million shekels; Bank Hapoalim, which rose 1.5 percent to 468 on turnover of 2.5 million shekels; and Bezeq Israel Telecom, which gained 1.5 percent to 810 on volume of 2.5 million shekels.
